prompt:
Task: HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1995 adventure game The Dig (LucasArts), in the smooth, detailed style approved for the main characters. This is a production asset. Every frame is fitted to the original frame's size and position afterwards, and the game lays it over the HD background with its own soft edges.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat cyan background (#00C8C8). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The border is only padding.

All frames on this sheet are animation frames of the same characters (Boston Low and Ludger Brink), as one scene, in different poses. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (1 frame); animation 6, facing right (4 frames).

Do:
- Repaint every frame in high resolution with clean, natural detail: smooth shading instead of dithering, smooth anti-aliased outlines (no pixel steps), believable cloth, skin, hair and material.
- Keep the original look: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast, in the painted style of the approved HD sheets.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and light in every frame. The frames are played one after another in the game, so any difference between them flickers.
- Keep the pose, proportions and silhouette of every frame as in the input, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, energy, lightning, sparks) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge or redesign frames. Do not add anything between the frames: no shadows, floor, text, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- Some frames show only part of the character, for example a body without a head or a head alone, because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Small bright magenta marks under the feet or at the edges are shadow markers used by the game. Leave them out; the game draws the shadow itself.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha, no background color and no gray border) and the frames in the same layout as the input. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing) as for the main characters.

If a second image is attached, it is an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take all poses and the layout from the first image.


TOM-AUTHORIZED SOURCE-BOUND STYLE CORRECTION, 10 OCTOBER 2026:
The actual original RGBA image controls all visible content. This costume is a COMPOSITE SCENE at the brown-red alien door, not separate people. Each numbered original source box must remain one composite drawing: retain the same dark rusty reddish-brown fan-shaped stone/door wedge, its stepped silhouette, slanted carved ribs, partial occlusions and cut-off boundary. Preserve only the visible Boston and Brink body parts/hands/heads in their exact original position, overlap and animation state. Never complete occluded or clipped people and never replace stone with a person. In fig230_01 the first four states contain only door/stone; the final state has tiny hands along the left edge. Other sheets show Boston above/behind the leaning blond Brink, as literally visible. Image TWO provides approved slim, long-nosed Brink FACE IDENTITY ONLY when a Brink face is actually visible. Image THREE is a face-only crop from the approved Boston sheet and provides Boston face and smooth drawing style ONLY when Boston is actually visible. Clothing, occlusion, palette, shape and poses come from imageONE; imageFOUR is the original final composite scene to confirm the two identities and door, not a new pose. ImageFIVE is a diagnostic numbered copy of imageONE; never paint its numbers or boxes. Smooth clean drawn detail and anti-aliased edges, no photographic textures, 3D rendering or invented chips/marks. Both men keep the original dark navy shirts and burnt-ochre trousers; only Brink wears the neutral gray jacket and straw-blond hair; Boston has brown hair. Keep the door identical across states apart from exact source deformation/occlusion. Remove pure magenta shadow markers only; keep real non-magenta source detail. True transparent alpha, no cyan/gray rectangle.
EXACT COMPOSITE DRAWING ROWS: [1, 4]; total 5. Never split a scene into separately placed people or door parts.

TARGET fig230_01: exactly five composite states in rows[1,4], all five showing the SAME dark reddish-brown grooved fan-shaped door wedge. Row1 one wedge. Row2 four wedges, with only the last wedge showing very small peach hand/finger pieces along its extreme LEFT cut edge (near y545 and y650 in native target). All other wedge states have NO visible people, faces, heads or bodies; do not add characters from the identity reference crops. Preserve the actual cuts/gaps in the wedge near its top-left and the straight cropped left/bottom edges. Palette dark maroon-brown in upper half, warm rust-brown along bottom ribs, no orange flames, new lights, cracks or decorative text. The wedge is a connected scene frame even if tiny hand pieces are disconnected. Same shape and rib pattern across all states. Native alpha required. Keep5 source states, not separate people.
